item.title: Small Resultant Systems via Linear Combinations
item.description: arXiv:2607.29308v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a system of $s$ homogeneous polynomials of degree $d$ in $n$ variables, say ${\bf{f}} = 0$, we consider the problem of constructing resultant systems. A resultant system is a finite set of polynomials in the coefficients of the input polynomials, the vanishing of which characterizes the systems $\bf{f}$ with a common non-zero solution. The classical approaches for constructing resultant systems rely either on maximal minors of large coefficient matrices or on the coefficients of a resultant of generic linear combinations of the input polynomials. Typically, they produce resultant systems containing a very large number of polynomials. We develop new constructions based on taking resultants of linear combinations of the input polynomials; this results in resultant systems of small cardinality. Our main results are: 1) We prove that a resultant system with ${d+n-1 \choose n-1} s-n^2+1$ polynomials exists; each polynomial is the resultant of $n$ linear combinations of the input polynomials. This improves the previously known upper bounds, even for systems of bivariate homogeneous polynomials. 2) Under the assumption that the input polynomials are non-zero, we construct explicit resultant systems with cardinality $\mathrm{poly}(s,d)$, when $n$ is fixed.
item.dc:creator: M. Levent Do\u{g}an, Elias Tsigaridas, Zafeirakis Zafeirakopoulos

item.title: Bounds on the second Hilbert coefficient and the depth of the associated graded ring
item.description: arXiv:2607.29311v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $(R, \mathfrak m)$ be a Noetherian local ring of dimension $d \geq 1$ with $\mathrm{depth} R \geq d-1,$ and let $I$ be an $\mathfrak m$-primary ideal. In this paper, we study bounds on the second Hilbert coefficient of $I$, denoted by $e_{2}(I)$. Under the assumption that the associated graded ring $G(I)$ has depth at least $d-1,$ we first establish a lower bound for $e_{2}(I).$ We then extend several known results from the Cohen-Macaulay case to this general setting and obtain upper bounds for $e_{2}(I)$ in terms of the sectional genus denoted by $\mathrm{g}_{s}(I)$ and the Hilbert coefficients of $I$ and those of a minimal reduction $Q$ of $I$. We further analyze the extremal case when $e_{2}(I)$ attains this bound and relate it to the depth of $G(I)$. In addition, for Buchsbaum local rings, we establish a sharp upper bound for $e_{2}(\mathfrak m)$ using the technique of $S_{2}$-fication. Finally, in the Cohen-Macaulay case, we give sufficient conditions to ensure good properties on the depth of $G(I)$ and of $G(I^n)$ under the assumption that $e_{2}(I)=0$.
item.dc:creator: Clare D'Cruz, Mousumi Mandal, Shruti Priya

item.title: The Hessian of elliptic curves as a Latt\`es map
item.description: arXiv:2407.17042v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that the Hessian transformation of elliptic curves, both as an action on $j$-invariants and on the Hesse pencil, is a rigid Latt\`es map fitting into a reduced diagram, hence it lifts to a degree-$3$ endomorphism $\psi$ of a prescribed elliptic curve $E$. This result provides an effective tool to investigate the dynamics of the Hessian transformation, whose symmetries are inherited from those of $\psi$, which we characterize. In particular, over arbitrary fields of characteristic different from $2$ and $3$, the functional graphs of the Hessian and, more generally, of Latt\`es maps fitting into analogous reduced diagrams, are completely determined by the action of $\psi$ on the twists of $E$. When the underlying field is finite, we specialize these results to obtain a complete classification of Hessian functional graphs and derive an efficient method for computing iterated Hessians.
item.dc:creator: Marzio Mula, Federico Pintore, Daniele Taufer
